title: Software Simulation Analysis of Integrating a Wake-Up Radio with a Bluetooth Low Energy Heart Rate Implant Sensor
content: This study explores the integration of Wake-Up Radios (WuRs) with Bluetooth Low Energy (BLE) bioimplant sensors to address the critical challenges of energy efficiency and operational longevity in Implantable Medical Devices (IMDs). Unlike previous studies, which predominantly examine Always-On WuRs or standalone duty-cycled BLE for WBAN, this work introduces and evaluates a novel Duty-Cycled WuR configuration specifically tailored for bioimplant systems. Through software simulations, three configurations are compared: standalone duty-cycled BLE, Always-On WuR-enabled BLE, and Du-ty-Cycled WuR-enabled BLE. The proposed Duty-Cycled WuR configuration demonstrates superior energy efficiency, significantly reducing cumulative power consumption while maintaining responsiveness for critical events. While this approach introduces a minor latency trade-off due to WuR sleep intervals, it is a reasonable compromise for extending the operational lifespan of energy-constrained IMDs.
